done_when: When Forge merges a branch, it merges its own record files itself (the higher round, the union of steps and reviews) instead of leaving a text conflict, and forge next names an unusable record and goes on for the other items; new and existing repos get it on upgrade

known.title: Disputed keep local state on equal rounds: story approvals are lost

Retain both concurrent blocking reviews in the active result

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - two machines review the same change and each reports a different blocking finding.
The merge selects only the first blocking snapshot as the current review; the other remains only in Git history. `src/forge/close.py:308` can reuse the selected review when the product files are unchanged, and its owner-acceptance path at `src/forge/close.py:138` accepts only that review’s findings. Close can therefore report the fix ready while the other blocker was neither addressed nor accepted. This breaks the repaired concurrent-review path.
findings.title: Retain both concurrent blocking reviews in the active result

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an active story’s local record becomes non-UTF-8 after its story branch has been published.
The new reader catches the invalid local record, but `_stories` can then restore the story from its valid committed ref and attach the same worktree at `src/forge/nextstep.py:575`. `_story` rereads that invalid file at `src/forge/nextstep.py:609`; `story._text` decodes it without handling the error. `forge next` exits before printing the refusal or the other items.
findings.title: Not done: Continue reporting for every unusable record

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - concurrent work adds steps on both machines.
The test’s only assertion that both step histories survived reads the private JSON record and compares its internal `steps` entries. The subsequent Forge command proves the resumed round, not the step union. An equivalent change to the record representation would break this test even if Forge’s observable behavior stayed correct; the step behavior still needs proof at a Forge command boundary.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_close_merges_records_with_the_higher_round_and_both_histories

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a committed unusable task blocks another task in the same story through overlapping scope.
The added blocker test always uses `OTHER/LOCK` against `SHOP/SAVE`, including its scope case. `src/forge/task.py:577` returns before reading a cross-story blocker, so this test does not exercise the repaired task-record reader. It would still pass if that reader again raised on malformed JSON, while a same-story scope blocker would terminate `forge next`. The command-level test needs that case.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_next_names_unusable_record_and_lists_other_items

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a repository previously set up with Forge upgrades to this release.
The new-repository case obtains the `up` fixture, which runs this checkout’s current `forge sync` before the upgrade (`tests/test_upgrade_command.py:143`). That already installs the new driver and attributes, so these assertions pass for that case even if upgrade fails to install them for an already-synced repository. The earlier-adoption case starts unsynced and does not cover that setup. Start the upgrade check with the previous release’s rules instead.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_upgrade_to_installed_release_continues_during_runs

why: When one fix is built on two machines, close merges the branch's remote and the fix's own record .factory/fixes/<fix>.json conflicts as text, leaving the checkout mid-merge; then forge next refuses for every item with '.factory/fixes/<fix>.json is not usable' (seen twice at a client on 18 Nov 2026)
